NO BLOCKERS

The Richmond recycling contamination audits candidate is publication-ready under the v4 local-news contract. What I verified:

- **Locality and freshness**: The story is anchored to Richmond with municipality-specific detail (grey glass bin, Richmond Recycling app, RecycleSearch tool). The City of Richmond notice (dated July 7 per its URL) appears in today's 12:30 primary-source discovery queue (`artifacts/editorial/research/2026-07-21-1230-primary-source-queue.json:250`), and the audits are active this month, so the July 21 publish time is current and actionable.
- **Reader utility and copy quality**: The bulletin delivers concrete reader jobs — audit timing, sticker feedback system, three sorting checks, and the lookup tool before collection day. `readerImpact` and `lengthRationale` are populated and match the format. At roughly 230 words there is no padding or hedged filler.
- **Primary-source support**: All specific claims (3% threshold, 7.3% curbside and 11.3% multi-family rates, 25% reduction by end of 2026, gold-star/"Oops" stickers) are attributed to the cited City of Richmond notice, whose URL matches the discovery queue entry exactly. The GPT evidence artifact verifies the candidate SHA-256 (`2915deed…3db2a9b`) against the exact hash supplied, with verdict PASS and factualSupport 5.
- **Em dashes**: A character-level scan of the file found zero em or en dashes; GPT's independent `proseEmDashCount` is also 0.
- **Source URLs**: Three well-formed URLs appear in both the body and the Sources section (richmond.ca notice, richmond.ca RecycleSearch page, recyclebc.ca guide).
- **Image**: I viewed `public/images/editorial/2026/07/richmond-recycling-contamination-audits.png` — blue bins with loose paper and cardboard plus separated glass bottles on a residential curb, matching the alt text and the story's sorting guidance, with no people or text artifacts, and attribution marked as original generated editorial imagery.
- **Commercial metadata and approval triggers**: `sponsorshipStatus: editorial`, `commercialIntent: ad-fit` with a reason correctly noting revenue signals are unavailable, `brandSafety: standard`, and all approval flags false. This matches the 12:30 scorecard, which also shows sensitive candidates (Richmond Oval forensic audits, Surrey enforcement items) were correctly held rather than published. Recycling audits are not a sensitive story and no sponsorship is involved, so no manual-approval trigger applies.

Two process notes, neither a blocker: the GPT review's `repositorySha` (`fde49ff`) is the parent of the staging commit because the review ran before the candidate was committed — the exact candidate-hash match confirms the reviewed content is identical to what's at `738f663`. And the prior Fable review artifact was recorded as `malformed_verdict` only because its verdict line was bolded; its substantive findings also identified no blockers.
